issue.title: Config schema and loader (single vault.toml + env overrides)
issue.body:
# Config schema and loader (single vault.toml + env overrides) — Issue #17 / M0-05

## Context

`vault` currently has no config layer — every subcommand is a stub. M0-07 (content-addressed
store) and M0-08 (journal) both depend on this ticket for `paths`, and six more milestones
(M2 thresholds, M3 proxy, M5 shared-library policy, M6 backup targets, M9 example configs)
build on the schema this ticket defines. The project's own history includes a real secret leak
(M0-02: Immich API key and DB password committed to three repos), so "no secrets in the file"
is a scar this design must actively defend against, not just document.

This is a greenfield repo with no existing `vault.toml` in the wild, so there's no backward
compatibility to preserve — the schema can be built in full now rather than staged behind
open decisions (M0-14 archive layout, M0-15 backup target choice).

## Decisions Made

Resolved in the planning session (recorded here; will also go into `docs/decisions.md` under M0-05):

- **Unknown keys are rejected** (pydantic `extra="forbid"`), to catch typos like `grace-days`
  vs `grace_days` immediately rather than silently falling back to a default.
- **Single shared `vault.toml`**, kept in sync across hosts by convention — no per-host
  `[hosts.<name>]` overlay. The canonical copy is expected to live on shared storage (e.g. the
  NAS) so both the Intel Mac and the NAS container read the same file. Path values that differ
  by host (e.g. local staging disk) are an operational concern for later, not solved by the
  schema in this ticket.
- **No general env-var override mechanism.** Env vars are used for exactly one thing: resolving
  named secrets (`*_env` fields). There is no `VAULT_<SECTION>__<KEY>` override for arbitrary
  config values — the user does not want a stray export able to change policy keys like
  `grace_days`. Tests construct `Config` objects or point `--config` at a fixture file rather
  than relying on env overrides.
- **`vault config show` never prints a resolved secret value** — it shows that a secret resolved
  and which env var it came from, never the value itself.
- **Validation: pydantic v2**, plain (no `pydantic-settings` — its env-loading machinery is
  unnecessary now that there's no general env-override feature). This is the project's second
  runtime dependency; `tomllib` (stdlib, Python 3.12) still handles TOML parsing.
- **All six schema sections ship now**: paths, sources, thresholds, proxy, publish, and backup —
  including a best-guess `backup.targets` shape, explicitly commented as provisional pending
  M0-15/M6-01. Being greenfield, there's no migration cost to revisit it later.
- **Secret resolution is implemented now**, not just prohibited: schema fields are named
  `*_env` (e.g. `immich.api_key_env = "VAULT_IMMICH_API_KEY"`), and the loader resolves them
  from the environment into a redacting `Secret` wrapper. macOS Keychain integration is
  explicitly deferred (no current consumer, and it can't work on the NAS's Linux container
  anyway) — noted as deferred in `docs/decisions.md`, not built.
- **`vault config validate` checks the filesystem**, not just the schema: it runs schema
  validation and then a preflight (paths exist/reachable, no overlapping paths). Schema loading
  itself stays pure (no filesystem access) so other commands aren't broken by an unmounted NAS
  when they don't touch that path.
- **AI-recommended, not explicitly discussed**: add a `schema_version` field and a stable
  canonical-serialization + hash on `Config`. This costs little now, and Contrarian Carl's
  finding stands: M0-08 (the very next ticket) builds the append-only journal that should record
  *which config governed a destructive batch* (e.g. `retire`'s `grace_days` / shared-library
  policy) — that hook is far cheaper to add at the same time as the loader than to retrofit into
  an existing journal format. Flagging this explicitly since it wasn't a direct answer to a
  question — if you'd rather defer it, it's a one-function removal.

## Approach

`tomllib.load()` parses the file into a raw dict; a single `load_config(path) -> Config`
boundary function feeds that dict into a frozen, nested pydantic v2 model tree with
`extra="forbid"` at every level. Constrained fields carry their constraints in the type
(`Literal` for `shared_library_policy`, bounded ints/floats for thresholds and quality,
non-negative `grace_days`), so illegal states can't parse. A dedicated error formatter turns
`pydantic.ValidationError` into the project's existing `vault: `name`: message` house style,
one line per error, on stderr. `vault config` becomes a real Typer sub-app with `show` and
`validate`, replacing its current stub registration.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: `src/vault/config.py` — schema and loader
- **What**: Pydantic v2 models: `PathsConfig`, `SourceConfig` (list), `ThresholdsConfig`,
  `ProxyConfig` (review/publish profiles), `PublishConfig` (`grace_days: NonNegativeInt`,
  `shared_library_policy: Literal["skip", "include", "include_no_retire"]`), `BackupTarget`
  (list, `kind: Literal["rsync", "restic"]`), top-level `Config` with `schema_version: int`.
  All models `frozen=True`, `extra="forbid"`. Path fields are `Path`, resolved
  (`expanduser().resolve()`) via a validator. A model-level validator on `Config` rejects
  mutually overlapping resolved paths (e.g. `staging` inside `archive`).
  Secret fields are declared only as `*_env: str | None` (e.g. `immich.api_key_env`), validated
  to look like an env var name (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`) — there is no field shape that accepts an
  inline secret value, so gitleaks becomes a second line of defense, not the only one.
  `load_config(path: Path) -> Config`: reads TOML via `tomllib`, validates via pydantic,
  resolves each `*_env` field via `os.environ` into a `Secret` wrapper (redacts in `repr`/`str`),
  raises a single `VaultConfigError` (in `errors.py`) wrapping all validation failures on
  failure — never returns `Config | None`.
  Add `fs_preflight(config: Config) -> list[str]`: checks configured paths exist/are reachable,
  returns problems as a list (empty = OK) — kept separate from `load_config` so it's opt-in.
  Add `Config.fingerprint() -> str`: stable canonical serialization + hash, for M0-08 to journal
  alongside destructive operations.
- **Why**: Tara's single typed boundary; Security Sage's structural secret prohibition and path
  overlap check; Carl's fingerprint hook; Nick's provisional-backup-schema labeling.
- **Files**: `src/vault/config.py` (new)

### Step 2: Error types
- **What**: Add `VaultConfigError(VaultError)` to `src/vault/errors.py`, carrying a list of
  `(key_path, message)` pairs. Add `CONFIG_ERROR = 2` to `ExitCode` (fills the existing gap
  between `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED=1` and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED=3`).
- **Why**: Config failures are a distinct exit condition from "not implemented" or "needs --yes".
- **Files**: `src/vault/errors.py`

### Step 3: Error formatting
- **What**: A formatter in `config.py` (or a small `errors.py` helper) that turns
  `VaultConfigError` into `vault: <config path>: <dotted.key.path>: <problem>` lines, one per
  error, matching the existing `vault: `name` ...` house style from `cli.py`. Applied both to
  pydantic validation failures and to `fs_preflight` results.
- **Why**: AC #1 — "fails fast with a clear message" — and Danielle's requirement that all
  errors are reported at once, not just the first.
- **Files**: `src/vault/config.py`, `src/vault/errors.py`

### Step 4: Wire `vault config` into the CLI
- **What**: Replace `config`'s stub registration in `COMMANDS` with a real Typer sub-app:
  `vault config show [--json]` (loads config via the existing `--config` global option,
  prints the effective config with secrets redacted to `<set from VAULT_...>` or `<unset>`);
  `vault config validate` (loads + runs `fs_preflight`, prints all errors, exits `CONFIG_ERROR`
  on any failure, `OK` otherwise). Bare `vault config` aliases `show`. `--json` on `show` is a
  deliberately cheap add now, since a future basic status/web UI (mentioned as a later goal, out
  of scope for this ticket) will want a structured read of the effective config.
- **Why**: `config` is already a registered stub pointing at issue 17; users will find it.
- **Files**: `src/vault/cli.py`

### Step 5: Example config
- **What**: `vault.example.toml` at repo root, covering all six sections with realistic but
  non-personal values (no real Mac/NAS paths — placeholders like `/path/to/archive`), backup
  section commented as provisional, thresholds commented as provisional pending M2-10
  calibration. `.gitignore` already ignores `vault.toml` but not `vault.example.toml` — no
  change needed there.
- **Why**: AC #2. Keeping it non-personal now avoids an M9-02 git-history scrub later.
- **Files**: `vault.example.toml` (new)

### Step 6: Record decisions
- **What**: Replace the M0-05 "Decision pending" stub in `docs/decisions.md` with the
  decisions listed above (pydantic v2 choice, single shared config file, no general env
  overrides, all sections shipped now, secret resolution now, keychain deferred).
- **Why**: Nick's point — these are exactly the framework decisions that get silently
  re-litigated in M0-08/M0-09 if unrecorded.
- **Files**: `docs/decisions.md`

### Step 7: Tests
- **What**: `tests/test_config.py` covering: valid config loads into `Config`; unknown key is
  rejected; path overlap is rejected; negative `grace_days` rejected; invalid
  `shared_library_policy` literal rejected; inline secret-shaped value has no valid field to
  populate (structural, so tested via "this key doesn't exist" rejection); `*_env` resolves
  from `os.environ` via monkeypatch; missing env var referenced by `*_env` produces a clear
  error; missing config file produces a clear "tried: ..." error; malformed TOML produces a
  clear error; `vault config show` output never contains a raw secret value; `vault config
  validate` reports a missing configured path via `fs_preflight`. Follow existing `CliRunner`
  patterns from `tests/test_cli.py` for CLI-level tests; use `tmp_path` fixtures for file-based
  cases.
- **Why**: mypy `strict` and the project's own bar (pre-push hook runs mypy + pytest).
- **Files**: `tests/test_config.py` (new)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **pydantic-core is a compiled dependency** — verified wheels exist for macOS (arm64/x86_64)
  and linux/amd64 (the NAS Docker target from M0-11), so this is low risk but worth confirming
  with `uv sync` on both platforms before merging.
- **Single shared config file across hosts with genuinely different valid paths** (Mac local
  staging disk vs. NAS-visible paths) is a real tension the user chose to resolve operationally
  (keep them in sync by convention) rather than in the schema. If this becomes painful once
  M7-02/M7-03 land, it's a schema addition, not a rewrite — `schema_version` exists specifically
  so that addition doesn't break existing configs.
- **Provisional `backup`/`thresholds` sections may be reshaped by M0-15/M2-10.** Since this is
  greenfield, that's an accepted, explicit cost, not a hidden one — both sections carry comments
  in `vault.example.toml` saying so.

## Testing Strategy

`uv run pytest` for the new `tests/test_config.py` plus the existing `tests/test_cli.py`
(unaffected except that `config`'s stub test case is removed from the generic stub-command
test and covered by the new CLI tests instead). `uv run mypy` for strict typing on the new
module. `uv run ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` for style. Manual verification:
`uv run vault config show` against `vault.example.toml` (via `--config`), and
`uv run vault config validate` against a config with a deliberately missing path to confirm
the fs_preflight error message.

## Out of Scope

- macOS Keychain integration for secrets (deferred, no current consumer).
- A `vault config init` command to scaffold a fresh `vault.toml` (first-run cliff noted, not
  addressed here).
- Any web UI / status dashboard (mentioned as a future desire; `--json` on `show` is a
  low-cost forward-compatible hook, not an implementation of that UI).
- Host-scoped config overlays (`[hosts.<name>]`) — explicitly rejected in favor of one shared
  file kept in sync by convention.
